voices.note: Mishnah Taanit 3:1 (18b), whose lemma is cited at 19a.12
the baraita of ורמינהי (19a.12): first and second rainfall to ask, third to fast
anonymous redactorial voice of this sugya

props.gloss_en: the mishna (lemma): the order of these fasts that is stated -- in the first rainfall
the baraita: the first rainfall [and the second] -- to ask
the baraita: [the first rainfall and] the second -- to ask
the baraita: the third -- to fast
Rav Yehuda: this is what it says -- the order of fasts stated, when? at a time when the first, second and third rainfall passed and rain did not fall
but if rain fell in the first rainfall and they sowed and it did not sprout -- they sound the alarm for them immediately
or else it sprouted and changed again -- they sound the alarm for them immediately
Rav Nachman: specifically 'changed'; but 'dried' -- no [they do not sound the alarm immediately]
it is needed where they produced stalks: one might say stalks are something of significance -- he teaches us [that even so, dried crops are not cause for the immediate alarm]

objections.gloss_en: ורמינהי: רביעה ראשונה ושניה לשאול, שלישית להתענות! -- the baraita puts fasting at the third rainfall, the mishna at the first (kind tanya under protest: the marker is ורמינהי)

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: the stated order applies when all three rainfalls passed without rain; in the first rainfall the case is rain that fell, was sown and did not sprout or changed -- for that they sound the alarm immediately (= p_yehuda_hachi_kaamar)
